scenario: a real estate listing platform tracking saved searches and inquiry rates
title: Premium Search Inquiry Minimum Price
prompt: You are working with a real estate listing platform modeled on public property datasets (e.g. Zillow Research Data, HUD USPS vacancy data). The platform tracks user searches and property inquiries. Searches are saved with a quality rating (1–5), and each search may match multiple properties with different inquiry prices. Write a query that finds, for each search that has a quality rating of 4 or higher, the cheapest inquiry price among all matching properties. For searches that do NOT meet the quality threshold, exclude them from the output entirely. The output must show: search_id, search_name (cleaned and capitalized), quality_rating, search_tags (the second tag only, using 1-based indexing), inquiry_month (the full month name from the earliest inquiry date), and min_inquiry_price (rounded to 2 decimal places). Order the results by search_id ascending.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE saved_searches (search_id INT PRIMARY KEY, search_name VARCHAR(200), quality_rating INT, search_tags TEXT[], created_date DATE); CREATE TABLE property_inquiries (inquiry_id INT PRIMARY KEY, search_id INT, property_id INT, inquiry_price_text VARCHAR(20), inquiry_date DATE);
answer_key: SELECT s.search_id, INITCAP(TRIM(s.search_name)) AS search_name, s.quality_rating, COALESCE(s.search_tags[2], '') AS search_tags, TO_CHAR(MIN(pi.inquiry_date), 'FMMonth') AS inquiry_month, ROUND(MIN(pi.inquiry_price_text::NUMERIC), 2) AS min_inquiry_price FROM saved_searches s JOIN property_inquiries pi ON s.search_id = pi.search_id WHERE s.quality_rating >= 4 GROUP BY s.search_id, s.search_name, s.quality_rating, s.search_tags ORDER BY s.search_id;
user_solution:
/* notes */

WITH base AS (
    SELECT
        s.search_id,
        INITCAP(TRIM(s.search_name)) AS search_name,
        s.quality_rating AS quality_rating,
        s.search_tags[2] AS search_tags,
        TO_CHAR(p.inquiry_date, 'FMMonth') AS inquiry_month,
        p.inquiry_price_text::numeric AS min_inquiry_price,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.search_id, INITCAP(TRIM(s.search_name)) ORDER BY p.inquiry_price_text::numeric ASC) AS rn
    FROM saved_searches AS s
    JOIN property_inquiries AS p
    USING(search_id)
    WHERE s.quality_rating >= 4
)
SELECT 
    search_id,
    search_name,
	quality_rating,
	search_tags,
	inquiry_month,
	min_inquiry_price
FROM base
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY search_id;
